story.title: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia

facts.text: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday .
Anthropic has signed a $44.6 billion contract for the project’s first building alone, according to Nscale’s IPO filing .

In essence, the chipmaker would be co-signing a customer’s loans, a sign of how hard the AI industry is working to keep its buildout plans afloat as investors grow jittery about the amounts of money involved.
Anthropic’s contract with Nscale covers the first 460-megawatt building at Nscale’s West Virginia campus, which is expected to use Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips.
The companies are also discussing a second deal worth roughly $45 billion for another building.

Under what’s known as a residual value guarantee, Nvidia would step in if Nscale defaulted on construction payments, temporarily take over the facility, and help find a buyer and new tenant, according to The Information .
Nscale has struggled to get its projects off the ground.
The company had about 25,000 advanced AI chips running in August , a fraction of the nearly 500,000 it plans to deploy.
Runoff from the construction site has flooded nearby homes more than once .
In September, after months of negotiations , the project won state certification.
The stakes are high for Nscale, which is seeking to go public at a valuation of up to $35 billion despite growing concerns about its ability to deliver on ambitious data center projects.
That includes $1 billion in convertible financing committed to Nscale in September.
Anthropic, one of the largest buyers of AI computing power, has spread its infrastructure spending across multiple chipmakers.
Nvidia’s earlier support for cloud providers has mostly covered leases and chip purchases, not construction.
This month, Microsoft pulled out of a planned Nscale site in England after grid power for it was pushed into the 2030s.
Nvidia is weighing an unprecedented move to cosign financing for Nscale's AI data center project in West Virginia, marking a dramatic shift in how chipmakers are supporting infrastructure buildout.
What was once easy money for data center projects has dried up, leaving companies like Nscale scrambling for creative financing solutions.
West Virginia has positioned itself as a low-cost alternative to traditional tech hubs, with abundant land and power capacity.
By cosigning the loan, the company would be taking on direct credit risk for a project that exists primarily to buy and deploy its chips.
The potential arrangement comes as investors grow increasingly nervous about the sustainability of AI spending, threatening to choke off capital for the very data centers that house Nvidia's chips.
For Nscale, landing Nvidia as a cosigner would be transformative.
